I like the idea of enforcing some minimum requirements for `Probe` statement but as written it still needs a lot of work.

Out of curiosity, did you try to see if we get less failures just checking for the manufacturer probe?

If that gets us started with fewer failures then maybe it could be worth achieving that first.

> Out of curiosity, did you try to see if we get less failures just checking for the manufacturer probe?

Presumably we would, but no, I didn't test that.

> 
> If that gets us started with fewer failures then maybe it could be worth achieving that first.


I prefer this patchset as written;  That gives us a way to enforce for new things and burn down over time.
Acknowledged

This is the copy-pasted existing function `remove_c_comments` from 
`scripts/validate_configs.py`
Yes, it is.  The function is the same.  It's not worth making a generic scripts utils class for two lines

We should not be duplicating code, even if it's just a single function.

If you duplicate this you are creating useless work for anyone reviewing the code who then needs to check if these functions are actually the same. 

Additionally there is a danger of code drift as people modify one function but forget to replicate the change here.

I can understand that if you are new to vibe coding you might have one-shot this without providing the coding agent with the existing code or instructing it to re-use instead of duplicating.

> We should not be duplicating code, even if it's just a single function.

We disagree.

> 
> If you duplicate this you are creating useless work for anyone reviewing the code who then needs to check if these functions are actually the same.

We're talking about two lines here in a 400 line patch.  If you think it's wrong, or doesn't match the existing, lets talk.

> 
> Additionally there is a danger of code drift as people modify one function but forget to replicate the change here.

Considering these are CI functions that are tested on every commit and only run on the repo, that's not a concern.  Code drift would result in an immediate CI failure.

> 
> I can understand that if you are new to vibe coding you might have one-shot this without providing the coding agent with the existing code or instructing it to re-use instead of duplicating.

It's not about the vibe coding aspect here, it's about keeping this script runnable in isolation.  Again, two lines, I'm not sure why we're arguing this.

If this were 50+ lines, I'd understand, but if we're going to deduplicate any 2 line stanzas, there's a lot more changes that need to be made common.
Acknowledged
This list should probably go into a separate file.
I prefer to keep it here.  Eventually this list goes away, so I'd like to keep this all in one file for now.
I would prefer it be broken out as a separate file. If you can't do that then at least don't put it in the middle of the code. Put the data at the top of the file and the actual code below then.
Moving to the top of the file is a fair ask.  I've done that in the latest patchset.

Let's get rid of this manufacturer matches folder stuff for now and let's start with a manufacturer match existing. If we have to make all these regex contortions to figure it out then it will be hard for folks to figure out why their changes are failing.

Overall the parsing here is conceptually wrong anyways since `Probe` is supposed to represent a boolean-ish conditional which needs an AST and proper parsing.

Creating complicated regex to work around that is an unstable shortcut which will likely introduce problems later on.

> Let's get rid of this manufacturer matches folder stuff for now and let's start with a manufacturer match existing. If we have to make all these regex contortions to figure it out then it will be hard for folks to figure out why their changes are failing.

Not interested in that.  The manufacturer matches stuff works as written, and as a maintainer I believe this script will help me maintain the folder structure.

Given the number of violations of this on code that was at one point reviewed, we need to have some kind of automation, and burn down list.

> 

> Overall the parsing here is conceptually wrong anyways since `Probe` is supposed to represent a boolean-ish conditional which needs an AST and proper parsing.

Agreed, this makes assumptions about the parsing, but I believe them to be correct assumptions that we will use positive matches, not NOT in a FRU probe.

> 
> Creating complicated regex to work around that is an unstable shortcut which will likely introduce problems later on.


Can you be more specific about the potential problems and what you think we should do here instead?  This is only a CI script.  If we have problems, we can always disable it (temporarily or permanently)

> Can you be more specific about the potential problems and what you think
 we should do here instead?  This is only a CI script.  If we have 
problems, we can always disable it (temporarily or permanently)

Let's

- write a real parser for probe statement (probably in c++)
- re-use that code then to create this tool

I don't like that we are duplicating things here and writing both the python and C++ code for parsing and processing the same thing. It's just writing everything twice and it will create a lot of work down the road for contributors.

Note that it will create extra work for you too since you will probably be reviewing that code as well.

> > Can you be more specific about the potential problems and what you think
>  we should do here instead?  This is only a CI script.  If we have 
> problems, we can always disable it (temporarily or permanently)
> 
> Let's
> 
> - write a real parser for probe statement (probably in c++)

Go right ahead.  Mine is in gerrit that I've pointed you to in the past.  In terms of this change, this parser is "good enough" to identify failures.  Also the actual EM implementation doesn't yet use a real parser, so holding this patchset to that.

As maintainer, if we in the future have false positives because of this I will go resolve them as part of my maintenance of this repo.  Of the files checked in, I've reviewed and I don't believe this to have false positives.

> - re-use that code then to create this tool

I'm in full support of this path, but it's not something I want to immediately execute on.  Is it something you want to do?  Functionally I'd really like to see all of this CI-script stuff moved to C++ built tools, but folks seem to like scripts (rightfully so) so for CI, generally I don't enforce that CI tools be in C++.

> 
> I don't like that we are duplicating things here and writing both the python and C++ code for parsing and processing the same thing. It's just writing everything twice and it will create a lot of work down the road for contributors.

Is this a position you're willing to put engineering behind?  The scripts folder has duplicated things at CI time in python for a long time.  Functionally this isn't making things much worse.

I agree, if we had C++ that could test all this stuff, it would run faster and likely be better, but that's not the status quo, and I'm not prepared to keep having this problem get worse while that solution gets engineered.

> 
> Note that it will create extra work for you too since you will probably be reviewing that code as well.

Yes, but it will be less work than having to constantly point out bad commits.  In terms of my personal tradeoff, I'd rather possibly have to revisit one script review than definitely have to revisit hundreds of reviews that get this stuff wrong on first patchset.  The goal is ultimately to make things get upstream easier, and I believe that on-balance, this patchset accomplishes that.

If you truly believe that this will make things harder to maintain, I'm happy to hear it, but from my perspective, it makes things easier.

> Is this a position you're willing to put engineering behind?

In the long term, yes, but i would put test coverage as a higher priority.
ACK.  If you're interested in the engineering, this is something I'm happy to even help with.  I also agree test coverage is an improvement worth doing.

Existing script already has all this code for collecting config files and paths.

Let's break that out and use a shared function instead of duplicating here.
I'd like to see scripts runnable in isolation. I'm not worried about this minor amount of code duplication in a CI script.

So it's wrong to re-use our own code?

You can still run the script if you import code from another python file. It's a common feature in python.

> I'm not worried about this minor amount of code duplication in a CI script.

I think you are taking too many shortcuts here. Whatever you merge will potentially stay in the repo for a long time and all contributors will have to work with it or work around it.


If is acceptable then what prevents us from duplicating 100-line functions?

Or copy-pasting entire applications like how it was done in dbus-sensors?

> So it's wrong to re-use our own code?

You're taking something said in the context of this specific line of code, and claiming I said it was some general rule.  In this specific context, I believe that not relying on the existing content is a good thing (to avoid the threadpool).

> 
> You can still run the script if you import code from another python file. It's a common feature in python.

True, but now I have to maintain dependencies cross script, as as stated elsewhere, I'm not at the point where I want to maintain this as anything other than one isolated test.

If we get to what you talk about elsewhere, where we have the "real" parser runnable as a c++ app, I agree, it makes sense to consolidate.

> 
> > I'm not worried about this minor amount of code duplication in a CI script.
> 
> I think you are taking too many shortcuts here. Whatever you merge will potentially stay in the repo for a long time and all contributors will have to work with it or work around it.

Absolutely right, I am taking shortcuts because I'm spending too much time reviewing incorrect patches and I need automation.  If you're interested in helping to refactor these things in the way you envision, I could really use the help.  I'm not against a lot of your ideas, just that I don't have time for it.

> 
> 
> If is acceptable then what prevents us from duplicating 100-line functions?

This is not duplicating 100 line functions, but to answer your question: Maintainers.

> 
> Or copy-pasting entire applications like how it was done in dbus-sensors?

I'm not going to debate the history of how dbus-sensors came to be in a single code review.  If you're interested, I'm happy to walk you through how that was allowed (hint, the maintainer wanted to support people merging code).  Ultimately what's there is now what the majority of people use, versus alternatives that enforced a lot more rules and were "cleaner" in design.  If you want to use those, I believe they're still available.
Acknowledged

I would prefer we integrate these checks with the existing logic. The existing logic has some `158     with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.threads) as executor:`

process pool thingy which Patrick did to avoid the delay of sequential processing.

> I would prefer we integrate these checks with the existing logic.

Is that something you'd like to put up a patch for?  I'm not against it, I just don't understand why we're worried in this context and it doesn't rise to the level of necessary for me.  As written, this script runs in 160ms for all configs on my machine.  For comparison, even with parallel execution, the schema check takes 2.0 seconds on the same machine, and 54 seconds user.  That difference is why the other one requires a pool and this one doesn't.


as an aside, I would be really curious to know why we even need a pool on validate_configs, and why it's so slow.  I'd bet we're scanning in the schemas for every iteration, and wouldn't need the pool there if we just read them in at the start, but that's a guess.
Acknowledged

Let's separate the script from the functions doing the work and modularize it in a separate file.

Currently the functions here cannot be re-used since there will be a name collision with another scripts `main` function.
Not interested in doing that.  This is functionally not that large of a script and separating out a bunch of utility classes makes this code seem like it's portable, which it is not.
Acknowledged
